title: Protocol for synthesis of di- and tri-substituted s-triazine derivatives
author: El-Faham, Sharma, et al.

steps.title: First substitution of cyanuric chloride
steps.instruction: Weigh 10 mmol cyanuric chloride (fuming solid) in the fume hood and dissolve it in 50 mL acetone in a conical flask. In a separate conical flask dissolve 10 mmol 4‑aminobenzonitrile in 50 mL acetone. Cool both solutions to 0 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mmol K2CO3 to the cyanuric chloride solution in a round‑bottom flask and stir vigorously at 0 °C.
Add the cold 4‑aminobenzonitrile solution dropwise to the stirring cyanuric chloride/K2CO3 mixture.
Stir the reaction for 4 h at 0 °C (temperature must be maintained to avoid double incorporation).
Monitor by TLC using 20 % MeOH in chloroform as the mobile phase in a closed system; proceed when no starting material is visible.
Quench by pouring the reaction mixture onto 1 L crushed ice in a beaker.
Filter the solid, wash with distilled water (3 × 500 mL), and dry the product under high vacuum to obtain the pure mono‑substituted triazine.

steps.title: Second substitution with aromatic/aliphatic amine
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mmol 4,6‑dichloro(1,3,5‑triazin‑2‑yl)aminobenzonitrile and 10 mmol of the chosen amine (piperidine, morpholine or diethylamine) each in 50 mL THF in separate conical flasks.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mmol K2CO3 to the dichloro‑triazine solution in a round‑bottom flask and stir vigorously at room temperature.
Add the amine solution dropwise to the stirring mixture of dichloro‑triazine and K2CO3.
Stir the reaction for 24 h at room temperature.
Monitor by TLC using EtOAc‑hexane (6:4) in a closed system; continue until the starting material disappears.
Remove THF with a rotary evaporator.
Pour the residue onto 1 L crushed ice.
Filter the solid, wash with distilled water (3 × 500 mL), and dry under high vacuum.
Recrystallize the crude product from ethyl acetate to obtain the purified 4‑[4‑chloro‑6‑substituted(1,3,5‑triazin‑2‑yl)amino]benzonitrile.

steps.title: Alternative first substitution using NaHCO₃
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mmol NaHCO₃ in water and cool the solution to 0 °C. Add 50 mL MeOH and stir vigorously at 0 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mmol cyanuric chloride to the cold MeOH/NaHCO₃ mixture while stirring.
Stir the reaction for 3 h at 0 °C (temperature must be maintained to avoid double incorporation).
Monitor by TLC using EtOAc‑hexane (6:4) in a closed system; proceed when no starting material is detected.
Remove excess MeOH with a rotary evaporator.
Pour the residue onto 1 L crushed ice.
Filter the solid, wash with distilled water (3 × 500 mL), and dry under high vacuum to obtain the pure product.

steps.title: Synthesis of 4‑chloro‑6‑methoxy triazine derivative
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mmol 2,4‑dichloro‑6‑methoxy‑1,3,5‑triazine and 10 mmol 4‑aminobenzonitrile each in 50 mL acetone in separate conical flasks.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.38 g NaHCO₃ (≈10 mmol) to the 2,4‑dichloro‑6‑methoxy‑triazine solution in a round‑bottom flask and stir vigorously at 0 °C.
Add the 4‑aminobenzonitrile solution dropwise to the stirring mixture of dichloro‑triazine and NaHCO₃.
Stir the reaction for 24 h at room temperature.
Monitor by TLC using EtOAc‑hexane (6:4) in a closed system; continue until the starting material disappears.
Remove acetone with a rotary evaporator.
Pour the residue onto 1 L crushed ice.
Filter the solid, wash with distilled water (3 × 500 mL), and dry under high vacuum to obtain the 4‑chloro‑6‑methoxy(1,3,5‑triazin‑2‑yl)amino)benzonitrile.

steps.title: Final substitution on methoxy‑chloro triazine
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mmol 4‑chloro‑6‑methoxy(1,3,5‑triazin‑2‑yl)amino)benzonitrile and 10 mmol 4‑aminobenzonitrile each in 50 mL acetonitrile in separate conical flasks.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mmol K2CO₃ to the chloro‑methoxy triazine solution in a round‑bottom flask and stir vigorously at room temperature.

Prepare a solution of the chosen amine (piperidine, morpholine, pyrrolidine, N‑methyl piperazine, 1‑amino ethanol, N,N’‑diethylamine, aniline, 4‑bromoaniline or 4‑methoxyaniline) in 10 mL acetonitrile; add this dropwise to the stirring mixture of chloro‑methoxy triazine and K2CO₃.
Reflux the reaction mixture for 18 h in an oil bath.
Monitor by TLC using EtOAc‑hexane (6:4) in a closed system; proceed when no starting material is observed.
Remove acetonitrile with a rotary evaporator.
Pour the residue onto 1 L crushed ice.
Filter the solid, wash with distilled water (3 × 500 mL), and dry under high vacuum.
Recrystallize the crude product from a 3:1 ethyl acetate‑ethanol mixture to obtain the final 4‑substituted‑6‑methoxy(1,3,5‑triazin‑2‑yl)aminobenzonitrile.

description: Method details involves synthesis of di- and tri- substituted s-triazine derivatives as drawn in below scheme. All the compounds were obtained in high yields and high purity as confirmed by 1H-NMR and 13C-NMR.
